repository_verification.verified_files_sha256_note: Digests as reviewed at repository.commit. Frozen evidence: do not rewrite them to make a suite green. A file that has knowingly moved since review belongs in accepted_drift_sha256 with a reason.

Written/ViewModels/DistillViewModel.swif.reason: Disconnect all now names both schemas, and three fixes around it. It deleted every local record including source='user', so a person who asked for their music and calendar to go came back to a profile with no school and no occupation; it now keeps what somebody typed, which is the same line SyncService.deleteEverything draws server-side. It then calls SemanticSurfaceService.forgetDistillation, the vault half that never existed — deleteEverything empties four tables in public and names none of the ones Memories reads, so every term stayed on that page after the sources behind it were gone. A failure there is reported separately and does not stop the local clearing, because the sources really are disconnected. distillationCleared is bumped so Memories reloads without waiting for a visit that never comes, Settings being raised from that screen. Also: runningSources drives the per-source distilling animation, which fired once for a batch and so looked absent on consecutive sources; and signOutLocalState clears ProfilePhotoCache beside ChatStore, other people's faces being held under an authorisation that ends with the session. No change to what leaves the device.

Written/Services/Ontology.swift.reason: A calendar term now reports its provider rather than its connector. `event.source` reads `apple_calendar` for an Outlook or Google account added in iOS Settings, because EventKit is how those arrive, so a term from an Outlook dinner claimed it came from Apple Calendar. It carries `event.provider`, read from the `cal_type` and `account` the distiller stamps; rows collected before that stamping read `other` rather than being guessed at.

Written/Services/SyncService.swift.reason: `deleteSource` now names both schemas. It deleted from `public.distilled_records` and `public.source_connections` and stopped there, so a disconnected source kept every observation and every encrypted record in the vault — measured 2026-08-15 on a real account that had disconnected Spotify: 580 active observations and 593 raw records still resolved, still scored, still read by the catalogue mint. It calls `api.forget_source` (0185) after the public half and returns the failure rather than swallowing it. The vault's own source code goes over the wire, asked of `SemanticSource.forAppSource` rather than reproduced, because `healthkit` and `health` are one of the two translation seams. The semantic side needs no change: the RPC is the semantic side.

Written/Models/DistilledRecord.swift.reason: SourceStatus gains `.partial(count:missing:)`. `.done` could not express "worked, and did not get everything", which is how a distillation that lost five of nine data types reported a count, grew the plant and told nobody. Measured on a device: consecutive runs carried four types and then nine. DistilledRecord itself is unchanged; the enum shares the file.

reference_migrations_note: Historical record of the standalone reference chain. Those files are deliberately NOT vendored into the Written repository: their adapted forms are application_migrations 42-47, and keeping both would be two divergent copies of the same DDL.
application_migrations_reserved_note: 50-57 carry the encrypted-vault path end to end: key registry, vocabulary alignment, the ingestion identity and its wrapped-key binding, key-write ordering, the run lifecycle, the finalize guard, and the worker identity that reads the vault back. 58 (server projections) is due in phase server_owned_discovery_and_profiles and 59 (cutover) in legacy_semantic_retirement. The pair has shifted nine times; the contract forbids reusing a number, not skipping one, so read a number in WRITTEN_REPOSITORY_INTEGRATION.md as the `role` below rather than as a filename. 59 is irreversible and must not exist on disk before a minimum supported client version does.
